terms.name: 3D tilt
terms.definition: Rotating a card in perspective toward the pointer so it appears to tip in three dimensions, often with a moving highlight to sell the depth.

terms.name: Active descendant
terms.definition: A focus technique where DOM focus stays on a container or input and aria-activedescendant names which child is active, used when focus must not move.

terms.name: APCA
terms.definition: A perceptual contrast algorithm proposed for WCAG 3 that scores a text and background pair as an Lc value and takes font size and weight into account.

terms.name: Audio control
terms.definition: A way to stop sound that started on its own, because autoplaying audio drowns out the screen reader voice a reader depends on to find the control that stops it.

terms.name: Biophilic design
terms.definition: A style that borrows from the natural world on purpose, using earthy greens and clays, organic silhouettes, botanical imagery, and slow ambient motion to make a screen feel less mechanical.

terms.name: Bulletproof button
terms.definition: A mail button built to survive a renderer that drops CSS: the fill carried by a cell or box behind the link rather than by a background the client can refuse.

terms.name: Categorical palette
terms.definition: A data palette of distinct hues at roughly equal visual weight, used for groups that have no order so no colour reads as larger than another.

terms.name: Chrome
terms.definition: The parts of a window or app that frame content rather than being content: title bars, toolbars, tab strips and address bars.

terms.name: Color interpolation
terms.definition: The rule for what happens between two colours in a gradient or transition, including which space the blend runs in and which way around the hue wheel it travels.

terms.name: Commitment pattern
terms.definition: The rare scanning shape where a motivated reader fixates on nearly every word, the only pattern that behaves like actual reading.

terms.name: Container color
terms.definition: A muted companion to an accent, light enough to fill a chip or a card behind ordinary text, so an accent can shade a region without shouting.

terms.name: Crossfade
terms.definition: A transition in which one element fades out while the other fades in over the same span, so both are partly visible at the midpoint.

terms.name: Dead zone
terms.definition: A range of input near the resting position that is deliberately ignored, so tiny unintended movement produces no response at all.

terms.name: Direct labeling
terms.definition: Writing series names next to the data instead of in a legend, trading a lookup for a glance.

terms.name: Drag autoscroll
terms.definition: Scrolling a container automatically when a drag is held near its edge, so an item can be moved somewhere currently off screen.

terms.name: E-ink aesthetic
terms.definition: A paper-like style built for or borrowed from electronic ink: near-white ground, pure black text, hairline rules, no shadows or gradients, and paged navigation.

terms.name: Entrance animation
terms.definition: The motion an element plays as it arrives, running from a starting style that only exists before the element was ever rendered.

terms.name: Fake door
terms.definition: A control that looks shipped and leads nowhere, put in the interface on purpose to count how many people want the feature behind it.

terms.name: First rule of ARIA
terms.definition: The maxim that no ARIA is better than bad ARIA: if a native element does the job, use it rather than pinning a role onto a div and reimplementing the behaviour.

terms.name: Fluid typography
terms.definition: Type sizes that scale continuously with the viewport between a minimum and a maximum, rather than jumping at breakpoints.

terms.name: Font smoothing
terms.definition: How a device softens the edges of letterforms, either by shading whole pixels grey or by lighting a pixel's colored subpixels separately.

terms.name: Gauge
terms.definition: A dial style readout showing one value on an arc between a minimum and a maximum, borrowed from instrument panels.

terms.name: Grid lanes
terms.definition: The native masonry mechanism in CSS grid, where one axis keeps strict tracks and the other lets items stack into whichever lane has room.

terms.name: Help drawer
terms.definition: Documentation opened beside the task rather than over it, keeping the form usable while the explanation is read and staying open across steps.

terms.name: Hub and spoke
terms.definition: A navigation shape where every task is reached from one home screen and returns to it, with no way to move sideways between tasks.

terms.name: Inert
terms.definition: A state that removes a subtree from focus order, hit testing, and the accessibility tree at once, used to seal the background behind a dialog.

terms.name: Intrinsic web design
terms.definition: Building layouts from what the content needs, using grid, flexbox and intrinsic sizing together, instead of imposing a fixed column skeleton.

terms.name: Keyboard key
terms.definition: A key drawn as a small keycap in running text or a menu, so a shortcut reads as something you press rather than something you say.

terms.name: Layout shift
terms.definition: Content moving after it has already been painted, usually because something arriving late took space that was never reserved for it.

terms.name: Lining figures
terms.definition: Numerals all drawn to cap height so they line up evenly with capitals and with each other.

terms.name: Lottie
terms.definition: A JSON format for vector animations exported from design tools and played natively on the web and mobile, so complex motion ships without video.

terms.name: Memphis design
terms.definition: The 1980s Memphis Group look of clashing pastels, squiggles, confetti dots, and terrazzo shapes scattered across a layout.

terms.name: Misdirection
terms.definition: Using contrast, size, and position to pull attention to the option the business prefers while the other option is present but visually demoted.

terms.name: Motion path
terms.definition: A defined path an element travels along, with its distance and rotation along that path animated instead of its x and y positions.

terms.name: Nested interactive
terms.definition: A focusable control placed inside another control, such as a button inside a link or a checkbox inside a clickable row, which garbles the announcement and can leave the inner control unreachable.

terms.name: Oldstyle figures
terms.definition: Numerals with varying heights, some rising and some dropping below the baseline, so numbers blend into lowercase running text.

terms.name: Ornament
terms.definition: A small panel of controls that floats just outside a window edge in visionOS, staying with the window without covering its contents.

terms.name: Pancake stack
terms.definition: A three row page where the header and footer take only the height they need and the middle row absorbs every remaining pixel, even when the content is short.

terms.name: Pixel art UI
terms.definition: An interface drawn on a visible pixel grid, with bitmap type, hard aliased edges, and icons kept at their original low resolution.

terms.name: Preselected opt-in
terms.definition: Arriving at a choice with the answer that benefits the business already ticked, so consent is collected from everyone who does not notice.

terms.name: Progressive reduction
terms.definition: Simplifying a control as the same person uses it more, dropping the label once the icon has been learned and restoring it after a long absence.

terms.name: Rag
terms.definition: The uneven edge left by unjustified text, and the thing typographers tune so that edge makes no distracting shapes down the side of a paragraph.

terms.name: Redundant entry
terms.definition: The rule against asking for the same information twice in one process, unless it is re-entered for a real reason such as confirmation.

terms.name: Ripple
terms.definition: A circular wash that spreads from the point of contact to acknowledge a touch, Material's way of tying feedback to where the finger landed.

terms.name: Scanlines
terms.definition: Thin repeating dark lines laid over an interface to imitate the raster of a cathode ray tube screen, often with a slight curve and flicker.

terms.name: Scrollbar
terms.definition: The bar beside a scrollable region whose thumb shows both how much content there is and where in it you are.

terms.name: Sender name
terms.definition: The name a mail appears to come from, chosen rather than inherited, because a reader scanning an inbox decides on it before reading a word of the subject.

terms.name: Site footer
terms.definition: The closing region of a site holding secondary navigation, legal links, and contact details that do not deserve top level placement.

terms.name: Social login
terms.definition: Signing in by delegating identity to an existing account elsewhere, presented as a row of provider buttons above or instead of a password form.

terms.name: Split screen layout
terms.definition: A page cut into two equal full height halves, each carrying its own message or path, with no hierarchy between them.

terms.name: Status color
terms.definition: The small fixed set of colours a product reserves for outcome, typically success, warning, danger and info, so meaning is consistent wherever it appears.

terms.name: Subgrid
terms.definition: A nested grid that borrows its parent's tracks instead of defining its own, so contents of separate children still line up with each other.

terms.name: Symbol support
terms.definition: Marking a control with a concept code so a reader who uses an augmentative symbol set sees their own familiar picture in place of your icon and wording.

terms.name: Text area
terms.definition: A multi-line text box, usually resizable, for input that will not fit on one line: a comment, a description, an address, a note.

terms.name: Title bar
terms.definition: The strip along the top of a window carrying its title and window controls, and the region you drag to move the window.

terms.name: Transfer list
terms.definition: Two side by side lists with arrow buttons between them, used to move items from available to chosen and back.

terms.name: Typographic hierarchy
terms.definition: The ordering of text by visual weight so a reader can tell at a glance what is a title, what is body, and what is a caption.

terms.name: Vibrancy
terms.definition: Apple's treatment where foreground colour is derived from the blurred content behind a material, so labels on a translucent panel shift with whatever they sit over.

terms.name: Widow
terms.definition: A short last line of a paragraph, often a single word, stranded at the top of the next column or page.

terms.name: Zoom transition
terms.definition: A presentation that scales a tapped element up into the full view it opens, so the destination appears to come from the thing that was touched.
